alternatives.why_less_likely: Errors observed in gateway are timeouts calling orders, not internal failures; no evidence of gateway internal error causing the slowdown.
High queue depth and pinned workers are consequences of payment‑induced timeouts, not an independent capacity loss.
Unanswered calls appear after orders already queued and are symptomatic of overload, not the initial failure.

causal_chain.claim: Payments responses became much slower than baseline.
Orders client calls to payments timed out due to the slowdown.
Orders server experienced increased latency and queuing as workers spent time waiting for payment timeouts (or retries).
Gateway timed out calling orders because orders was slow to respond.
User‑visible errors appeared as 504 timeouts at the gateway entry point.

root_cause.summary: Payments service became significantly slower, causing callers to time out and propagate failures upstream.

verification.reason: disabling the matching condition(s) makes the incident disappear

alternatives.why_less_likely: Payments showed gradually rising latency rather than immediate failures, and no config change events are recorded.

causal_chain.claim: Payments service latency increased sharply (p99 rose from ~1.4s to >3.7s).
Orders timed out when calling payments and scheduled retries.
Payments entered load‑shed state due to excessive load.
Gateway timed out when calling orders and returned 5xx errors.
Users observed 5xx errors as err5xx spiked in gateway metrics.

root_cause.summary: Payments service experienced increased latency, causing downstream timeouts and retries.
